title: Weighted Average Rebuilt Old Total Before Adding New Scores
text: id: COMP-003 domain: math title: Weighted Average Rebuilt Old Total Before Adding New Scores tags: weighted-average, average, total memory: A grade problem once tricked me because I treated an old average like one old score. The fix was to recover the hidden total first: old average times old count. Only after that did the new scores belong in the sum. When I divided by the full new count, the gradebook and my answer finally agreed.

title: Average Speed Used Total Distance Over Total Time
text: id: COMP-002 domain: math title: Average Speed Used Total Distance Over Total Time tags: average-speed, rate, time memory: I once averaged two speeds directly and got a smooth wrong answer. The trip log exposed it: speed was distance divided by time, not the average of the speed labels. I computed each leg's time, added the distances, added the times, and divided total distance by total time. The answer felt less tidy but it matched the road.

title: Ratio Mixture Counted Total Parts Before Liters
text: id: COMP-009 domain: math title: Ratio Mixture Counted Total Parts Before Liters tags: ratio, mixture, parts memory: A mixture ratio felt like two numbers competing until I counted total parts. Two parts and five parts made seven equal chunks of the final volume. I found liters per part first, then multiplied by each side of the ratio. The concentrate and water added back to the requested total.
